info.name: Send Transactions API
info.description:
REST API collection for SEND_TXN_OWNER schema.

Writes flow exclusively through the Kafka canonical pipeline
(POST /api/publish). The REST surface (v1 + v2) is read-only —
GET-by-id only. Older PUT / DELETE / list endpoints have been
removed.

Base URL and tranIds are collection variables — edit them under
the Variables tab.

variable.description: tranId used by the v1 read-only endpoint. Defaults to the id produced by the Kafka publish examples (K1).
tranId used by the v2 read-only endpoint. Defaults to the id produced by the Kafka publish examples.
Per-row ID of a SEND_TRAN_ADDR_DTL record. Use the id from v2-Q1's addrDtl[] to fetch a single address.

item.name: Kafka Publish (insert / upsert path)
item.description:
Publishes an EventEnvelope to the Kafka topic via POST /api/publish.
This is the ONLY write path — there are no REST PUT/DELETE endpoints.

Structure:
  EventEnvelope          — outer wrapper (validated: all fields @NotBlank / eventTimestamp @Positive)
    └─ eventPayload      — JSON-string of TransactionEventAxonMessage

The consumer deserialises both layers, applies the YAML canonical mapping
for the eventName, then upserts SEND_TRANSACTIONS + child tables.

Returns 202 Accepted on success; 400 Bad Request when @Valid fails.

request.description:

item.name: K2. PAYMENT_COMPLETED — status update (re-upsert same tranId)

request.description: Same tranId=TXN-PAY-001 re-upserted with status=COMPLETED. The MERGE null-guard preserves all fields already in DB that are absent from this payload.

item.name: K3. PAYMENT_FAILED — error event

request.description: PAYMENT_FAILED event creates TXN-PAY-002 with status=FAILED, error ERR-5001, network response 51.

item.name: K4. FUNDING_INITIATED — full funding payload → saves to DB

request.description:
FUNDING_INITIATED event → matched by FUNDING.yaml → tranIdSource=fundingId → DB key=FUND-001, tranType=FUNDING.

Expect logs:

  [CONSUMER] Canonical request built | tranId=FUND-001 tranType=FUNDING
  [CONSUMER] Saved to DB successfully

item.name: K5. FUNDING_SETTLED — funding completion update

request.description: Re-upserts FUND-001 with fundingStatus=SETTLED. Null-guard preserves all previously saved fields.

request.description:
AIS event sourced from src/test/resources/testdata/AIS/AIS_COMPLETE.json.

Populates every settable column of the four canonical-mapping tables:
  - SEND_TRANSACTIONS
  - SEND_TRAN_DTL
  - SEND_RECIP_DTL
  - SEND_TRAN_ADDR_DTL (SENDER + RECIPIENT rows)

Use for an e2e read-back: after publishing, GET
/api/v2/send-transactions/tran_complete-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-000000000001
to see the full nested graph.

item.name: K7. ignore=true — skipped by consumer (no DB write)

request.description: ignore=true stops the consumer after logging the envelope. No mapping or DB write occurs.

item.name: K8. Unknown eventName — no mapping (warning logged, no DB write)

request.description:
eventName=UNKNOWN_EVENT_TYPE has no YAML mapping. Consumer logs a WARN and skips DB write.

To handle this event: add 'UNKNOWN_EVENT_TYPE' to the eventNames list of an existing YAML, or create a new UNKNOWN_EVENT_TYPE.yaml.

item.name: K9. 400 — Validation failure (missing required envelope fields)

request.description: Missing eventName, eventId, correlationId, eventMetadata, eventPayload (@NotBlank) and eventTimestamp (@Positive defaults 0). Expects 400 with field-level validation errors.

item.name: K10. BLOCKED — eventSource not in allowedEventSources (PAYMENT)

request.description:
eventSource=UNKNOWN_SOURCE is NOT in PAYMENT.yaml allowedEventSources=[AIS_SERVICE, PAYMENT_HUB].

Rule engine fires at Step 4 (after routing, before payload deserialization).

Expect logs:
  [CONSUMER]  Matched mapping | eventType=PAYMENT
  [RULE ENGINE] IGNORED | rule=eventSource | value='UNKNOWN_SOURCE' | allowed=[AIS_SERVICE, PAYMENT_HUB]
  [CONSUMER]  Message blocked by rule engine

No DB write. Returns 202 to the publisher (Kafka is fire-and-forget).

item.name: K11. BLOCKED — operation not in allowedOperations (PAYMENT)

request.description:
eventSource=AIS_SERVICE passes Rule 1. But operation=D is NOT in PAYMENT.yaml allowedOperations=[A, U].

Rule engine fires at Step 4, Rule 2.

Expect logs:
  [CONSUMER]  Matched mapping | eventType=PAYMENT
  [RULE ENGINE] IGNORED | rule=operation | value='D' | allowed=[A, U]
  [CONSUMER]  Message blocked by rule engine

No DB write. Compare with FUNDING.yaml which DOES allow operation=D.

item.name: K12. RECTIFIED — malformed payload fixed and saved to DB

request.description:
eventPayload uses single quotes and has a trailing comma — both are not valid in strict JSON.

Sanitizer fires at Step 5:
  Attempt 1 (as-is)      → FAIL  (not valid strict JSON)
  Attempt 2 (trim)       → FAIL  (still invalid)
  Attempt 3 (unwrap)     → FAIL  (doesn't start with '"')
  Attempt 4 (lenient)    → PASS  → re-emits strict RFC-8259 JSON

Expect logs:
  [SANITIZER] eventPayload is not valid JSON — starting rectification attempts
  [SANITIZER] Rectified ✓ | strategy=LENIENT_RESERIALIZE
  [CONSUMER]  Canonical request built | tranId=TXN-SAN-001
  [CONSUMER]  Saved to DB successfully

item.name: K13. IRRECOVERABLE — truly invalid payload, message skipped

body.raw:
{
  "regulatoryRegion": "US",
  "eventSource": "AIS_SERVICE",
  "eventName": "PAYMENT_INITIATED",
  "eventId": "EVT-SAN-002",
  "correlationId": "CORL-SAN-002",
  "eventTimestamp": 1731660600000,
  "eventMetadata": "{\"operation\":\"A\",\"timestamp\":\"2025-02-04T12:30:00Z\"}",
  "eventPayload": "THIS IS NOT JSON AT ALL *** CORRUPT PAYLOAD ***"
}

request.description:
eventPayload is plain text — no rectification strategy can recover it.

Sanitizer fires at Step 5:
  Attempt 1 (as-is)      → FAIL
  Attempt 2 (trim)       → FAIL
  Attempt 3 (unwrap)     → FAIL  (doesn't start with '"')
  Attempt 4 (lenient)    → FAIL  (not parseable even leniently)

Expect logs:
  [SANITIZER] eventPayload is not valid JSON — starting rectification attempts
  [SANITIZER] eventPayload is irrecoverable — message will be skipped. Preview: THIS IS NOT JSON...
  [CONSUMER]  eventPayload is invalid and cannot be rectified — skipping

No DB write. Returns 202 to the publisher (Kafka is fire-and-forget).

item.name: K14. CLEARING_SETTLED — full payload (source-side field names)

request.description:
CLEARING is the 2nd leg of a dual-message transaction. Run K1 (PAYMENT_INITIATED) FIRST to populate the parent SEND_TRANSACTIONS row for tranId=TXN-PAY-001, THEN run this request to populate the 5th table SEND_TRAN_CLRG_SETLMT for the same tranId.

Note the eventPayload uses SOURCE field names (clearingStatus, clearingDate, acqRefNumber, rateTypeIndicator, reasonCode, reasonCodeDesc) — these match TransactionEventAxonMessage. The canonical-mapping engine renames them to the DB-aligned target fields per CLEARING.yaml's clrgSetlmt: block.

Flow:
  1. Consumer deserialises payload → TransactionEventAxonMessage
  2. Engine applies CLEARING.yaml clrgSetlmt: mappings → SendTranClrgSetlmtRequest
  3. Service checks parent SEND_TRANSACTIONS row exists
  4. Service MERGEs into SEND_TRAN_CLRG_SETLMT

Expect logs:
  [CONSUMER]  Matched mapping | eventType=CLEARING
  [CONSUMER]  CLEARING request built | tranId=TXN-PAY-001 clrgSt=SETTLED
  [CLEARING] Upserting SEND_TRAN_CLRG_SETLMT for tranId=TXN-PAY-001
  [CLEARING] Upsert complete for tranId=TXN-PAY-001

item.name: K15. CLEARING_INITIATED — minimal required source fields only

request.description: Minimal CLEARING_INITIATED payload — only the NOT-NULL targets (tranId, clrgSt, clrgDtTs) are supplied via the source-side field names (clearingStatus, clearingDate). All other columns remain null.

item.name: K16. CLEARING — missing tranId (rejected by service)

request.description:
eventPayload omits tranId. The tranIdSource lookup falls back to envelope.correlationId — but if you also clear correlationId the request is rejected by the service.

In the actual default config the correlationId fills tranId, so this case in practice will use CORL-CLRG-003 as tranId and then fail the parent-existence guard (see K17). Use this entry to confirm the fallback behaviour.

item.name: K17. CLEARING — unknown tranId (no parent row → logged & skipped)

request.description:
tranId=TXN-DOES-NOT-EXIST-999 has no parent row in SEND_TRANSACTIONS (the PAYMENT event never arrived). Service checks parent existence first and silently drops the message.

Expect logs:
  [CONSUMER]  Matched mapping | eventType=CLEARING
  [CLEARING] No parent SEND_TRANSACTIONS row for tranId=TXN-DOES-NOT-EXIST-999 — message ignored (expected the PAYMENT event to have arrived first).

No DB write.

item.name: K18. SETTLEMENT — populates settlement columns (source-side field names)

request.description:
SETTLEMENT is the 3rd leg of a dual-message-style flow. Run K1 (PAYMENT_INITIATED) FIRST to populate the parent SEND_TRANSACTIONS row for tranId=TXN-PAY-001. Then run K14 (CLEARING_SETTLED) to populate the clearing columns. Finally run this request to merge the settlement columns into the SAME SEND_TRAN_CLRG_SETLMT row (PK=TRAN_ID).

The eventPayload uses source-side field names (setlDt, setlAmt, setlCurrCd, setlServId, setlIca, tranFileId) which map identically to the target field names in this case. clearingStatus / clearingDate are also propagated so the row stays consistent.

Expect logs:
  [CONSUMER]  Matched mapping | eventType=SETTLEMENT
  [CONSUMER]  SETTLEMENT request built | tranId=TXN-PAY-001 clrgSt=SETTLED setlAmt=1500.00
  [SETTLEMENT] Upserting SEND_TRAN_CLRG_SETLMT for tranId=TXN-PAY-001
  [SETTLEMENT] Upsert complete for tranId=TXN-PAY-001

item.name: K19. SETTLEMENT — unknown tranId (no parent row → logged & skipped)

request.description:
Same guard as CLEARING — tranId=TXN-DOES-NOT-EXIST-998 has no parent SEND_TRANSACTIONS row, so the service drops the message after a single WARN log.

Expect logs:
  [CONSUMER]  Matched mapping | eventType=SETTLEMENT
  [SETTLEMENT] No parent SEND_TRANSACTIONS row for tranId=TXN-DOES-NOT-EXIST-998 — message ignored.

No DB write.

item.name: Send Transactions API (v1) — Read-only
item.description:
Read-only v1 surface at /api/v1/send-transactions.
The only operation is GET-by-id; writes go through the Kafka publish path above.

item.name: 1. GET by ID - Full Graph

request.description: Returns the full nested graph: parent + tranDtl + recipDtl + addrDtl[].

item.name: 2. 404 - GET Non-Existent ID

request.description: Expects 404 Not Found from GlobalExceptionHandler.

item.name: Metadata-Driven API (v2) — Read-only
item.description:
Read-only v2 surface at /api/v2/{alias}/{id}.

Only route:
  GET /api/v2/{alias}/{id}    fetch with nested children

Writes and discovery endpoints have been removed — writes flow exclusively
through the Kafka publish path; schema details live in src/main/resources/metadata/.

Aliases come from the YAML files under src/main/resources/metadata/:
  send-transactions  send-tran-dtl  send-recip-dtl  send-tran-addr-dtl

item.name: Query Operations
v2-Q1. GET by ID - Full Graph

request.description:
Response is a Map<String,Object> assembled from the YAML metadata:
  - parent columns at the root
  - tranDtl   → nested Map (or null)
  - recipDtl  → nested Map (or null)
  - addrDtl   → array of Maps

Field order follows the YAML column order (LinkedHashMap).

item.name: Direct Child-Table Access
item.description: Because every table is registered with its own alias, child tables are addressable on their own — useful for ops queries that don't need to walk through the parent.

item.name: v2-C1. GET send-tran-dtl by tranId (PK=FK)

request.description: SEND_TRAN_DTL has PK = FK = TRAN_ID. The {id} path variable is the tranId.

item.name: v2-C2. GET send-recip-dtl by tranId (PK=FK)

request.description: Returns the SEND_RECIP_DTL row (sender + recipient PII, DOBs as ISO yyyy-MM-dd).

item.name: v2-C3. GET single address by its UUID

request.description: SEND_TRAN_ADDR_DTL has a per-row PK (ID). Use the id returned in v2-Q1's addrDtl[] array — the collection variable {{addrIdV2}} points to one.

item.name: Error Cases
v2-E1. 404 - GET non-existent id

request.description: Returns 404 with the same ErrorResponse shape (UTC timestamp + traceId from MDC) as v1.

item.name: v2-E2. 500-ish - Unknown alias (no YAML registered)

request.description: MetadataRegistry.require throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown alias. Caught by the generic exception handler — 500 with a masked message ("An unexpected error occurred"). Real error visible in server logs.
